key_insight: HiAR introduces hierarchical denoising for autoregressive diffusion: by conditioning on multi-scale, partially denoised contexts rather than fully clean frames, the model preserves uncertainty and prevents progressive error accumulation, enabling longer coherent video generation.
problem_solved: Addresses progressive quality degradation and temporal discontinuity in autoregressive long-video generation caused by conditioning on overly denoised contexts that propagate errors with high certainty.
method: Hierarchical denoising pipeline: generate and denoise video context at multiple temporal scales (coarse-to-fine) to stabilize long-range temporal structure.
Uncertainty-aware conditioning: use partially denoised / stochastic context representations instead of fully cleaned predictions to avoid overconfident error propagation.
Efficiency strategies: autoregressive scheduling in compact latent or grouped-frame space to reduce compute while maintaining temporal continuity.
impact: Makes autoregressive diffusion practical for long-form video by reducing error accumulation and improving temporal consistency, enabling higher-quality, scalable video synthesis for research and production use cases.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing hierarchical denoising: coarse level → intermediate → fine, with arrows indicating partial conditioning at each stage.
Side-by-side frame sequence comparison: baseline AR diffusion (degrading) vs HiAR (consistent) across many timesteps/frames.
Schematic illustrating conditioning effects: fully denoised context (high-confidence error propagation) vs partially denoised context (uncertainty preserved).
Chart: quality (FID/PSNR/consistency) vs generated video length showing slower degradation for HiAR.
paper_title: HiAR: Efficient Autoregressive Long Video Generation via Hierarchical Denoising
paper_authors: Kai Zou, Dian Zheng, Hongbo Liu, Tiankai Hang, Bin Liu
